category_notes.text: Krita AI Diffusion documents using a selection as an inpainting mask. A useful design check is whether the change stays inside the selection while the surrounding layer remains usable.
Kdenlive 26.08 documents configuring speech recognition and object detection separately. Caption timing and tracked masks can be treated as separate post-production passes.
Audacity's OpenVINO plugin distribution distinguishes separation, noise suppression and transcription. Each effect should be checked against the actual audio output and its platform package.
Microsoft's TRELLIS.2 project demonstrates image-conditioned generation of textured 3D assets. Downstream checks still need to cover topology, material channels and export behavior.
Transformers.js documents opting into WebGPU in a browser. A browser tool's usefulness depends on the selected model, its download and the browser's execution backend.
Nerfstudio documents a web viewer for inspecting trained scenes and creating camera paths. Headset compatibility needs its own evidence for any shortlisted workflow.
The ml5 learning material includes 3D pose estimation for creative sketches. It gives creative coders a way to drive motion and visualization with model keypoints.
The ml5 demos and guides provide browser inputs for live hand and body interaction. The pose or gesture model is one component in the interactive work, with latency and tracking still to evaluate.
CADAM's project site describes turning text into editable CAD. A generated design needs a separate fit, dimensions and geometry check before studio fabrication.
The Hugging Face Godot RL Agents course documents training agents against game environments. It makes controlled NPC behavior a distinct creative task from generating level art.
FreeMoCap documents moving a tracked recording into Blender, including FBX and BVH export options. Rig retargeting and retiming remain separate checks after capture.
NVIDIA's Audio2Face-3D release describes audio-driven facial animation. Model terms, required runtimes and the target character's facial rig need to be checked for each integration.
The SAM 2 project shows that a click, bounding box or mask can initialize a tracked video object mask. Check edges and occlusions before handing masks to compositing.

SoundSpaces 2.0 describes generating spatial sound responses for arbitrary source and listener positions in a scene. The cited work supports acoustic simulation research, with DAW interchange still to verify.
LichtFeld's documentation describes selecting and deleting splats after reconstruction. A clean cropped view and the exported representation are separate handoff checks.
Subtitle Edit 5 documents Windows, Linux and macOS and several local and cloud speech-to-text engines. Model scope and precise timing can be checked separately from editor compatibility.
StarVector publishes SVG examples generated from image or text inputs. Editable paths, readable type and viewBox behavior still need inspection for production art.

FontDiffuser describes adapting to a glyph style with very little reference material. Its published work addresses glyph images. Font file construction, spacing and licensing require their own workflow.
Koharu's project site describes combining detection, OCR and inpainting for comic translation. Inspect balloon fit, reading order and the selected translation model before using a page.

Presenton describes generating, editing and exporting presentations. The current project overview is available. One deeper configuration URL returned 404, so detailed model configuration remains a gap in this field check.
RapidRAW documents ONNX Runtime for local masks and distinguishes its optional generative replacement route. That difference matters when choosing a local raw-photo workflow.
FiftyOne documents embedding visualization for media datasets. An embedding projection is useful for browsing similar images and outliers when its model and inputs are documented.

The ml4a ConvnetOSC guide documents sending learned feature activations over OSC and a first-hand installation example. An OSC mapping makes the model output available to an installation's control software.
Magenta's DDSP VST project documents using a learned timbre model in a plugin and training a personal model. Host compatibility and latency determine how it fits into a live set.

The GarmentDiffusion paper describes multimodal generation of garment sewing patterns. The source provides a research route for the field. Fit, seam alignment and the software grant are separate screening steps.
Kdenlive's speech-to-text documentation gives a practical captioning path. Timestamp accuracy, speaker names and layout still need human review before using the captions in accessible media.
Apple documents converting Stable Diffusion checkpoints to Core ML and deploying with Swift on Apple platforms. Android integration follows a separate runtime and model-conversion path.

Machine Learning for Kids provides practical learner projects. The reviewed software path trains a small classifier and exposes its output to a Scratch project, so the classifier can be checked against held-out examples.
eScriptorium documents editing page segmentation and OCR or handwriting transcription in the browser. That separates machine-assisted recognition from the final transcription and its archival export.

Ghent CDH documents IIIF enrichment through Madoc, including multilingual transcription, entity annotation and image segmentation. The specific enrichment service needs its own license and model check.

Oxford VGG's WISE documentation describes free-text search in video, audio and automatically generated transcripts. Matching candidates give archivists a way to find the relevant frame or segment before verifying the source material.

Sony CSL's NOTONO project publishes examples of local changes to selected spectrogram regions. The developer examples establish a creative interface for the task. A before-and-after listening check is still needed for a restoration claim.

Subtitle Edit documents multiple transcription backends and subtitle editing. For documentary localization, check subtitle cue boundaries before and after translation, then keep a sidecar with the original timecodes.

Qwen-Image-Layered decomposes a flattened image into separate RGBA layers. Its research artifacts explain layered editing. Check layer order, partly hidden regions and the destination format before handing off artwork.
The e-baton research documents learned conducting-gesture recognition. Wekinator's published interaction examples show another route for mapping learned gestures to live media controls.

CMU reports research on translating images into touch. The Stanford prototype link returned 404 in the direct source check. PreFigure documents tactile rendering as a downstream diagram format, with learned conversion and embossing evidence still separate.

SDPS-Net documents separate lighting estimation and surface-normal estimation from multiple images. Its result can assist detailed surface inspection. Relightable materials require additional capture and validation.

Madoc documents adding annotations and transcription to IIIF objects. Ghent CDH describes image segmentation and entity enrichment work, which can help a curator build narrative context without changing the master images.
